questions: Does the README (given in <readme>) still describe the code correctly after this change: endpoints, responses, settings, commands?
Does a new route, setting, command or public function need a line in the README or docs?

hints.title: New endpoint {1} isn't in the README
hints.titleWithoutReadme: New endpoint {1}, but no docs changed
hints.why: People using the API look for endpoints in the README, so a missing one is invisible to them.
hints.fix: Add {1} to the README, with what it takes and what it returns.
hints.comment: Could you add {1} to the README so people know it exists?

hints.title: New setting {1} may not be documented
hints.why: Someone setting up the project won't know {1} exists until something fails.
hints.fix: Add {1} to .env.example (with an empty value) or to the README.
hints.comment: Could {1} go in .env.example or the README, so new setups know to set it?
